narration: Nine out of ten purchases you make aren't logical — they're emotional. Your brain pulls the trigger before your logic even wakes up. Wild, right?
visual: Split brain SVG: left half labeled LOGIC in blue, right half labeled EMOTION in glowing orange. Dollar signs float upward out of the emotion side. Dark background.

narration: Stress is trigger number one. When cortisol spikes, your brain reaches for instant relief — and that usually means spending. Retailers literally track these patterns.
visual: Person silhouette with red stress ripple circles radiating outward. A credit card slides into their right hand. A shopping bag floats in from the right. Light background.

narration: Celebration is just as sneaky. Hit a milestone and your brain says you deserve a reward — it's called self-gifting, and it averages $1,200 per event.
visual: Happy person silhouette with arms raised, a golden trophy beside them, and a receipt growing taller. Dollar counter ticks up to $1,200. Dark background.

narration: Then there's boredom buying. Scientists found 23% of all online purchases happen when people just have nothing to do. And it gets worse.
visual: Person lounging on a couch holding a phone with a shopping app. A cart badge fills up with items from 0 to 5. Zzz indicators float above. Light background.

narration: Retailers spend $18 billion a year studying your emotional state. Those countdown timers and 'only 3 left' badges hit you in a 6-second window before logic kicks in.
visual: Detailed phone screen mockup showing a sneaker product page with countdown timer ticking 6 to 1, a red 'ONLY 3 LEFT' badge, and a pulsing BUY NOW button. Dark background.

narration: Here's your fix: wait 24 hours before any unplanned purchase. That one pause saves the average emotional spender $14,000 a year. Follow for more tricks like this.
visual: Clock face with rotating hour hand labeled 24 HRS, an arrow pointing right to a growing pink piggy bank with a coin dropping in. Savings counter ticks up to $14,000. Light background.
